sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Nutrition & Health** encompasses the study of macro and micro-nutrients, balanced diet, deficiency diseases, and metabolic functions.
Core syllabus component tested frequently in **UPSSSC PET General Science** section.
Applicable across all human biological processes, immunity building, and disease prevention.
Essential for aspirants preparing for **Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission (UPSSSC)** exams.
Directly scores 2-3 questions in the PET exam covering vitamins, deficiency disorders, and **Balanced Diet** components.
Classification of nutrients into **Carbohydrates, Proteins, Fats, Vitamins, and Minerals** with specific chemical names and deficiency symptoms.
High-yield scoring area with direct factual questions on chemical names of vitamins and mineral functions.
Covers both water-soluble and fat-soluble vitamins, calorific values of food, and common communicable/non-communicable diseases.

items.title: Carbohydrates and Fats (Energy Foods)
items.content:
• **Carbohydrates:** Primary source of energy, composed of Carbon, Hydrogen, and Oxygen in a **2:1 ratio** of H to O.
• **Classification:** Monosaccharides (Glucose, Fructose), Disaccharides (Sucrose, Lactose, Maltose), and Polysaccharides (Starch, Glycogen, Cellulose).
• **Fats (Lipids):** High energy yielding biomolecules providing **9.3 kcal/g** compared to **4.1 kcal/g** from carbohydrates.
• **Saturated vs Unsaturated:** Saturated fats (butter, ghee) are solid at room temperature; unsaturated fats (vegetable oils) are liquid.
• **Mnemonic for Fat-Soluble Vitamins:** **ADEK** (A, D, E, K dissolve in fat).

items.title: Proteins (Body Building Foods)
items.content:
• **Composition:** Polymers of **Amino Acids** linked by **peptide bonds** containing Carbon, Hydrogen, Oxygen, Nitrogen, and sometimes Sulphur.
• **Essential Amino Acids:** Cannot be synthesized by the human body; must be obtained through diet (e.g., **Lysine, Leucine**).
• **Non-Essential Amino Acids:** Synthesized within the body (e.g., **Alanine, Glycine**).
• **Deficiency Diseases:** **Kwashiorkor** (protein deficiency with adequate calorie intake) and **Marasmus** (overall protein-energy malnutrition).
• **Mnemonic for Essential Amino Acids:** **PVT TIM HALL** (Phenylalanine, Valine, Threonine, Tryptophan, Isoleucine, Methionine, Histidine, Arginine, Leucine, Lysine).

items.title: Vitamins and Their Chemical Names
items.content:
• **Vitamin A:** **Retinol** | Deficiency: **Night Blindness (Nyctalopia)** and Xerophthalmia.
• **Vitamin B Complex:** Group of water-soluble vitamins essential for cellular metabolism and RBC formation.
• **Vitamin C:** **Ascorbic Acid** | Deficiency: **Scurvy** (bleeding gums).
• **Vitamin D:** **Calciferol** | Deficiency: **Rickets** in children and Osteomalacia in adults.
• **Vitamin E:** **Tocopherol** | Deficiency: **Sterility** and fragile RBCs.
• **Vitamin K:** **Phylloquinone** | Deficiency: **Non-clotting of blood**.
• **Mnemonic for B-Complex Vitamins:** **ThRiyP NC PBiF** (Thiamine B1, Riboflavin B2, Niacin B3, Pantothenic acid B5, Pyridoxine B6, Biotin B7, Folic acid B9, Cobalamin B12).

items.title: Minerals and Deficiencies
items.content:
• **Calcium:** Required for bone/teeth formation and blood clotting | Deficiency: **Tetany and Osteoporosis**.
• **Iron:** Core component of **Hemoglobin** | Deficiency: **Anemia**.
• **Iodine:** Essential for **Thyroxine** hormone synthesis | Deficiency: **Goitre** (enlargement of thyroid gland) and Cretinism.
• **Sodium & Potassium:** Maintain fluid balance and nerve impulse transmission.
• **Fluorine:** Prevents dental caries | Excess causes **Fluorosis**.
• **Mnemonic for Major Minerals:** **C I S P F** (Calcium, Iron, Sodium, Potassium, Fluorine).

items.title: Balanced Diet and Deficiency Diseases
items.content:
• **Balanced Diet:** Contains all essential nutrients in correct proportions (Carbohydrates 60-70%, Proteins 15-20%, Fats 20-25%).
• **Malnutrition:** Condition resulting from lack of one or more nutrients.
• **Protein-Energy Malnutrition (PEM):** Affects infants and young children primarily in developing nations.
• **Water & Roughage:** Crucial non-nutrient components; water constitutes **60-70%** of adult human body weight.
• **Mnemonic for Disease Classification:** **C-D-V** (Communicable, Deficiency, Viral/Bacterial).

items.definition: Remember the sequence for A, B1, B2, B3, B5, B6, B9, B12 using: **Rath par ek nirogi panti phasi** (Retinol, Thiamine, Riboflavin, Niacin, Pantothenic, Pyridoxine, Folic, Cyanocobalamin).
Think of the word **KDE A** or **ADEK** — Vitamins **A, D, E, and K** dissolve in fat and can be stored in the liver.
Remember **BC** — Vitamins **B and C** are water-soluble and excreted through urine daily, requiring regular dietary intake.
Use **C-P-F** (**C**alcium, **P**hosphorus, **F**luoride) as the core triad for skeletal strength and dental health.
**K**washiorkor = **K**ids with pot bellies due to pure protein deficiency; **M**arasmus = **M**uscis emaciation due to total starvation (protein + calories).
Vitamin B3 (Niacin) deficiency causes Pellagra remembered by **4Ds**: **D**ermatitis, **D**iarrhea, **D**ementia, and **D**eath.

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing Vitamin B1 and B12 Deficiency
items.definition: Vitamin B1 deficiency causes **Beriberi**, whereas Vitamin B12 deficiency causes **Pernicious Anemia**. Do not mix up neurological beriberi with blood disorders.
Students often think all vitamins are stored in the body. Only **fat-soluble (A, D, E, K)** are stored in the liver; water-soluble ones (**B and C**) are flushed out.
Kwashiorkor occurs when calorie intake is adequate but **protein is missing**. Marasmus occurs when **both calories and protein** are severely lacking.

items.term: Mistake 4: Calorific Value of Fats vs Carbohydrates
items.definition: Fats yield more than double the energy (**9.3 kcal/g**) of carbohydrates (**4.1 kcal/g**), but carbohydrates are used as the **immediate primary fuel** by cells.
**Scurvy** is caused by Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid) deficiency (bleeding gums), while **Rickets** is caused by Vitamin D deficiency (bone softening).
Goitre is caused by the deficiency of **Iodine**, not Iron. Iron deficiency specifically causes **Anemia**.
Carbohydrates, Proteins, and Fats are required in large quantities for energy and tissue construction.
Vitamins and Minerals are required in trace amounts but are vital for metabolic regulation and disease resistance.
Crucial for visual pigment (**Rhodopsin**) synthesis in retinal rod cells.
Synthesized in human skin upon exposure to **Ultraviolet (UV) rays** from sunlight acting on cholesterol precursors.
Essential for the synthesis of **prothrombin** in the liver, enabling blood coagulation.
Composed of amino acid chains linked by peptide bonds; serves structural, enzymatic, and hormonal functions.
An optimal diet balances energy yield, tissue repair catalysts, and protective micronutrients.
Dietary fiber (cellulose) adds bulk to food and facilitates smooth bowel movements.
Acts as the universal solvent regulating body temperature and metabolic transport systems.
Iron binds oxygen in red blood cells; its deficiency reduces oxygen-carrying capacity, leading to fatigue.

upscNotes.content: UPSSSC PET frequently asks direct matching questions between vitamins and their chemical names or deficiency diseases. Memorize the Vitamin table thoroughly.
Focus on the calorific value figures (Fats = 9.3 kcal/g, Carbohydrates = 4.1 kcal/g) as numerical data points appear in science MCQs.
Exam traps often interchange 'Retinol' and 'Calciferol' or 'Thiamine' and 'Riboflavin' options. Double-check chemical names before marking.
Do not assume water-soluble vitamins can be stored in excess; regular dietary replenishment is mandatory.

keyTakeaways: Carbohydrates and fats are energy-yielding macronutrients, whereas proteins are body-building blocks.
Fat-soluble vitamins are A, D, E, K; water-soluble vitamins are B-complex and C.
Vitamin B1 deficiency causes Beriberi, Vitamin C causes Scurvy, and Vitamin D causes Rickets.
Kwashiorkor stems from protein deficiency; Marasmus stems from overall protein-energy starvation.
Iodine deficiency causes Goitre, while Iron deficiency causes Anemia.
Fats provide more than twice the energy per gram compared to carbohydrates.
